buildings.name: Vitthala Temple
buildings.summary: A temple complex where carved granite halls frame the celebrated chariot-shaped Garuda shrine.
buildings.history: Developed under Vijayanagara patronage, the complex forms part of Hampi's sacred landscape. Its buildings reflect successive phases rather than a single construction event.
buildings.layout_notes: An enclosure brings together the main shrine, pillared halls and the chariot-shaped shrine. Architectural details reward close inspection of individual pillars and pavilions.

materials.notes: Carved structural pillars and the Garuda shrine; not a claim that every component is granite.

buildings.name: Chennakeshava Temple
buildings.summary: A Hoysala temple whose platform and sculpted surfaces create a close encounter with stone craftsmanship.
buildings.history: Worship at the Belur temple is documented from 1117 CE. It belongs to the UNESCO-listed Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas and remains an active religious place.
buildings.layout_notes: The circumambulatory platform allows the exterior to be experienced as a sequence of carved surfaces. The present form also reflects changes and losses over time.

styles.name: Hoysala
styles.notes: One of the three ensembles identified by UNESCO.

elements.name: Sculptural frieze

elements.notes: Carved bands form part of the exterior treatment.

citations.note: 1117 CE records inception and continuity of worship, not the completion date of every component.

buildings.name: Virupaksha Temple
buildings.summary: A Dravida temple at Pattadakal, commissioned by Queen Lokamahadevi around 740 CE.
buildings.history: The temple commemorates the military success of Lokamahadevi's husband. Its location within the Pattadakal ensemble makes it a useful point of comparison with neighbouring temple forms.
buildings.layout_notes: The southern architectural tradition is expressed in the temple's shrine and superstructure. Sculpture is integral to its architectural treatment.

elements.notes: The district source identifies several sculptural subjects.

buildings.name: Badami Cave 3
buildings.summary: A rock-cut shrine with a dated inscription and a richly carved pillared verandah.
buildings.history: An inscription records the creation of the shrine by Mangalesha in 578 CE. The cave is part of Badami's group of four principal cave temples.
buildings.layout_notes: A pillared entrance space leads into the excavated interior. Large relief panels and carved bracket figures are important parts of the architectural experience.

styles.name: Rock-cut
styles.notes: Excavated temple architecture rather than assembled masonry.

materials.name: Sandstone
materials.notes: The cave is excavated into Badami's sandstone cliff.

elements.name: Sculptural relief

buildings.name: Durga Temple
buildings.summary: An apsidal temple with an open colonnade, a columned hall and finely worked stone screens.
buildings.history: ASI assigns the monument broadly to the seventh–eighth centuries CE. Its name should not be used by itself to infer the temple's original religious dedication.
buildings.layout_notes: A rounded shrine end and surrounding passage distinguish the plan. An open colonnade, hall and porch establish a sequence between the exterior and the shrine.
